engine-definition.statement: A DLP engine is a collection of one or more DLP dictionaries, and any mix of cloned, predefined and custom dictionaries can be added to one.

quotes: A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) engine is a collection of one or more DLP dictionaries.
Any combination of cloned, predefined, and custom dictionaries can be added to a DLP engine

rules-reference-engines.statement: DLP policy rules and Endpoint DLP policy rules must reference engines, not dictionaries. To use a custom dictionary in a rule, put it in an engine first.

quotes: When you define your DLP policy rules and Endpoint DLP policy rules, you must reference DLP engines, rather than DLP dictionaries.
Any combination of cloned, predefined, and custom dictionaries can be added to a DLP engine, which is what you must reference when creating DLP policies.

api-rule-has-engines-only.statement: The Web DLP rule object carries a `dlpEngines` list and no field for dictionaries, so the indirection is an API-level requirement as well as a console one.
api-rule-has-engines-only.conditions: Rests on an absence in the Go SDK rule struct and the API reference's request fields for the add-rule operation: neither lists a dictionary field. Search: the field names of `request_body` for zia/data-loss-prevention/web-dlp-rule-resource-add-rule contain no name matching `dictionar`.

quotes: // The list of DLP engines to which the DLP policy rule must be applied.

predefined-engines-exist.statement: Zscaler provides predefined engines (the Match Only example names a PCI engine and a HIPAA engine) and supports custom ones. An admin can edit or clone a predefined engine as well as create a custom engine.

quotes: The Zscaler service provides predefined DLP engines and supports custom DLP engines.
You can edit predefined engines, create custom engines, or clone existing engines
For example, you create a DLP rule with the PCI engine and select the Match Only option. In this case, the rule does not trigger when a transaction triggers both the PCI and HIPAA engine.

boolean-composition.statement: An engine combines dictionaries with Boolean operators into a logical expression. The API expresses this as `engineExpression`, using All (AND), Any (OR), Exclude (NOT) and Sum (the total number of content matches).

quotes: you can also combine dictionaries with Boolean operators to create logical expressions

expect.description:
The logical expression that defines a DLP engine by combining DLP dictionaries using logical operators, namely All (AND), Any (OR), Exclude (NOT), and Sum (the total number of content matches). .

Engine expression examples:

  • ((D63.S> 1))
  • ((D38.S> 1) AND (D63.S> 1))
  • ((D38.S> 1) OR (D63.S> 1))
  • ((D38.S> 0) AND ( NOT ( (D61.S> 0) ) )
  • (SUM(D63.S, D38.S)> 3)

In the preceding examples, 63 represents the ID of the Credit Cards dictionary ID, 61 is the Financial Statements ID, and 38 is the ABA Bank Routing Numbers dictionary ID. Each dictionary ID is wrapped around by a prefix (D) and a suffix (.S).

expression-wire-form.statement: On the wire an expression references dictionaries by ID, each wrapped in a `D` prefix and an `.S` suffix and compared with a number, for example `((D63.S > 1) AND (D38.S > 0))`. The engine object stores the expression as one string; it has no separate list of dictionaries.

quotes: zia.dlp.validate_dlp_expression("((D63.S > 1) AND (D38.S > 0))")

operators-and-root.statement: Engine expressions use the operators All (AND), Any (OR), Exclude (AND NOT) and Sum; Sum sets the total number of matches that triggers a group of dictionaries and is available for count-based dictionaries such as Credit Cards and Social Security Numbers. The root expression allows only All, Any and Sum, and a subexpression cannot be added to an expression or subexpression that uses Sum, though Sum can be used inside a subexpression.

quotes: The operators include All (AND), Any (OR), Exclude (AND NOT), and Sum. The Sum operator allows you to specify the sum total of matches that trigger a group of dictionaries specified in the DLP engine.
You can use the Sum operator as part of a subexpression; however, you cannot add a subexpression to an expression or subexpression that uses the Sum operator.
The Sum operator is available for count-based DLP dictionaries (e.g., Credit Cards, Social Security Numbers.)
For the root expression, only the All (AND), Any (OR), and Sum operators are allowed.

operators-and-root.conditions: Help words Exclude as AND NOT while the API reference's engineExpression description words it as Exclude (NOT); the API's own example `((D38.S> 0) AND ( NOT ( (D61.S> 0) ) )` combines AND with NOT, so this is a wording difference, not a conflict.

match-count-semantics.statement: The match count is the threshold that triggers a dictionary or group of dictionaries, and they trigger only when they find more matches than the number entered: with Sum over 3 dictionaries and a count of 6, the policy triggers at 7 or more matches across them. With multiple dictionaries each carrying its own count, a dictionary triggers only when its own threshold is reached. One dictionary can sit in several engines with a different count in each.

quotes: The match count is the threshold that triggers a dictionary or group of dictionaries.
The dictionary or dictionaries trigger only if they find more matches than the number specified.
If you use the Sum operator in your expression with 3 dictionaries, and you enter a match count of 6, then the policy triggers only if there are 7 or more matches across the 3 dictionaries.
If you select multiple dictionaries with individual match counts, the dictionary is triggered only when the threshold is reached for an individual dictionary.
You can add a dictionary to multiple engines and specify a different match count value each time you add a dictionary to an engine.

confidence-set-in-dictionary.statement: A predefined dictionary's Confidence Score Threshold is set in the dictionary itself, not in the engine.

quotes: To modify the Confidence Score Threshold of a predefined dictionary, you must configure this setting in the dictionary itself.

builder-limits.statement: In the engine builder, Sum needs two or more dictionaries and a match count; All, Any or Exclude need a dictionary, and certain dictionaries require a match count. A match count is any value less than 1,000. Each level allows up to 4 subexpressions, 4 operators and 16 dictionaries per operator, and an engine description cannot exceed 255 characters.

quotes: If you use the Sum operator, select two or more predefined or custom DLP dictionaries. You must set a value for the match count. You can enter any value less than 1,000.

If you use the All, Any, or Exclude operators, you must select a predefined or custom DLP dictionary. Certain dictionaries require you to set a value for the match count. You can enter any value less than 1,000.
At each level, you can create up to 4 subexpressions, use up to 4 operators, and add up to 16 dictionaries per operator.
The description cannot exceed 255 characters.

parent-sub-in-engines.statement: When an engine uses a parent dictionary a sub-dictionary can also be selected, and must be when the parent has no patterns or phrases. Parent and sub-dictionaries in an engine are evaluated separately and can match independently; sub-dictionaries appear in brackets in the expression.

quotes: If the parent dictionary doesn't have patterns or phrases defined (i.e., it is being used simply as a container for sub-dictionaries), then you must select a sub-dictionary from the drop-down menu.

channels-required.statement: Creating or editing an engine requires selecting a channel, and excluding a channel can reduce noise from engines used unnecessarily. Channels can also be overridden from the DLP Engines list, but a channel cannot be removed from an engine used in an active policy.

quotes: Excluding a channel can reduce the extra noise that comes from engines being used unnecessarily.
When creating a DLP engine, you must select a channel.
When editing a DLP engine, you must select a channel.
You can optionally override the channels associated with an engine directly from the DLP Engines page:
You can't remove a channel from an engine that is used in an active policy.

api-expression-unparseable.statement: If an expression sent through the API is broken or not recognized, even though it is correct in form (the page says "synthetically correct"), the console's engine builder cannot parse it: the Edit DLP Engine window shows it in a Reference Expression field and displays a blank Engine Builder section, and the expression must be recreated by hand. The page's examples of unparseable expressions are (D63.S > 0 AND NOT D39.S > 0), (D63.S > 0 OR NOT D39.S > 0 AND NOT D125.S > 0) and (SUM(D63.S, D246.S) > 2).

quotes: If the expression sent for the DLP engine through the API is broken or not recognized, even though it is synthetically correct, the engine builder cannot parse the dictionary.
In this case, you need to manually recreate the expression in the Edit DLP Engine window in the Zscaler Admin Console.
In the Edit DLP Engine window, the expression that could not be parsed is displayed in the Reference Expression field and a blank Engine Builder section is displayed.
(D63.S > 0 AND NOT D39.S > 0)
(D63.S > 0 OR NOT D39.S > 0 AND NOT D125.S > 0)

clone-engine.statement: Any predefined or custom engine can be duplicated (cloned) to copy its functionality for a different use, with a name specified for the new engine.

quotes: You can duplicate a predefined or custom Data Loss Prevention (DLP) engine if you need to easily copy the functionality of an existing engine for a different use.
In the Clone DLP Engine window, specify a name for the new engine.

expression-threshold-meaning.title: What the number in a dictionary term such as D63.S > 1 compares against
expression-threshold-meaning.blocks: stating that the API's .S term is the console's match count
expression-threshold-meaning.detail: Narrowed by match-count-semantics: the Understanding DLP Engines page, now captured, says the console's number is a match count and that dictionaries trigger only when they find more matches than it. channel-scoping-semantics.title: Whether a channel association limits where an engine triggers
channel-scoping-semantics.blocks: saying that a channel-scoped engine never fires on inline web traffic
channel-scoping-semantics.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "an engine can be scoped to specific channels ... engines scoped to them only trigger on that traffic type. Inline (web) DLP engines don't need channel scoping." The help page lists channels as a column on the engines table; no captured source says a channel association restricts an engine to that channel, or that an engine without channels is inline-only.
